Wheelchair Boxer

By: Hamilton Wende | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fighter who won't give up on his dreams.. even from a wheelchair

Unique Selling Point:
Adesanya “Tony” Adebayo is a man who won’t let life beat him. And he doesn’t particularly like other people beating him either. This Nigerian immigrant to South Africa contracted polio as a child which made his left leg extremely weak, forcing him to use a wheelchair as his main way of going about the world.

Summary:
He is a fighter who won't give up on his dreams. He wakes early in the morning in Johannesburg and begins training. He begins with push up and sit-ups and then does laps around the block of his Turffontein home.
Tony is a competitive wheelchair sprinter and mid-distance competitor, as well as a champion weightlifter.
His real dream, though, is unique. He wants to be South Africa's first competitive wheelchair boxer. When he's not working at the hair salon which is his day job, and where, despite his handicap, he stands for most of the day, he is at the gym training with his coach and able-bodied boxers, learning how to box better and how to pit himself against opponents who have so many advantages over him.
His life is a voyage of self-discovery, where, as he says, "You want to be a champion, but not a champion for yourself, but a champion for others too." He works hard at the salon and develops himself into as multifaceted a human being as he can be. He attends church, plays the saxophone and trains to beat himself and the handicaps that he carries bravely with him.
He hasn't persuaded sporting authorities to recognise wheelchair boxing yet, but he is not giving up on his dream. He trains, boxes at the gym and competes in racing and weightlifting in the South African Sports Association for the Disabled championships (SASAPD) in wheelchair racing and weightlifting, keeping his many goals alive and working towards his ultimate challenge.
Like all disabled people, he too, has times when things have seemed difficult, perhaps even unmanageable, but he refuses to give up.
In this way he hopes to touch people's lives and inspire them to better their own and to find a way to fight for their own dreams.
Living in SA for more than a decade and he sends money home to his wife and children in Nigeria, and he says South Africa is a land of opportunity, a place where he has been able to follow his dreams.
Tony will be competing in the SASAPD championships in late March so we will spend a day with Tony, starting early in the morning on Friday 10 March, filming him and interviewing him as he goes about his day, from training in the early morning to playing the sax to going to the salon and the gym where he trains and boxes with other able-bodied opponents.
Then on March 21 we will film him at the final day of the SASAPD championships down in Cape Town where he competes in the 800m wheelchair race and the final results are announced. He may not win the actual race, but this will provide a nice narrative arc to follow him through his journey into his own success and his personal best.

https://www.sasapd.org.za/

Script:


Dawn.
At the hard edges of a dream.
While most people are sleeping

Tony Adesanya is fighting for a vision.
Struck by polio in his home country Nigeria at the age of 2, Tony has learned to live with his disability
Cut to Tony’s soundbite “This is my calliper. I use it once in a while because sometimes when I’m walking my leg just flip to the front..

The virus attacks nerve cells in the spinal cord and brain stem controlling muscle movement.
It spreads through contaminated water, which Tony believes is how he contracted the disease. Often one or more legs are paralysed - exactly what happened to Tony.

Still, despite his limitations, he is determined to make the most of what life offers him.
His legs are too weak for normal sports - his upper body is the only part of him that functions normally. And a wheelchair makes it possible for him to compete.
He trains every day before the traffic gets too busy, strengthening his upper body, seeking always to better himself.
And a few weeks ahead lies a major test for Tony. He is training to win medals in the South African Sports Association for the Physically Disabled championships down in Cape Town a few weeks from now.

Shots of Tony doing push ups etc cut to drone shot..
Its opportunities like these which Tony celebrates in South Africa.
Back in Nigeria, from childhood on, he tried to prove himself, but he found it too difficult to succeed.
Originally he wanted to emigrate to Europe, but instead, he found South Africa, what he calls a real land of opportunity, where people embraced him, and his disability, and helped him to start again.
Shots of Tony calling home

But he still misses home every day..

“Hello boy how are you I miss you so much… yeah all right always pray for daddy okay?”

His wife, Adeola, sells palm oil at the market, but the money is not enough to bring up his two boys, Bomi and Ademiga, properly. Tony grew up poor and Cut to soundbite cc 5664 05:53:40 “What’s good about my job is that I meet a lot of people.. cut to 05:53:47 trying to know more about life and talking to people makes me feel free and have confidence in myself.” 05:53:57

Mac Piece to camera 04:52:23 “Tony Adesanya came here to better his life but he soon found out that in these gritty Johannesburg streets, he could fulfil his dreams, and that’s despite his life long handicap.”

Montage of Tony playing the sax .. DRIVE 2 FOLDER TONY ADESANYA JOBURG CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW 29:30 onwards also DRIVE 1 TONY ADESANYA CARD1 FOLDER 5651 ONWARDS also DRIVE HW 2 CARD 1 towards end of Max cutaways 04:33:18 onwards
While aggressively chasing medals, Tony also strives for a balanced life. Before work every morning, he makes time to feed his soul, playing the saxophone.

DRIVE 2 CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW… Mac 00:25 When you start playing it, where does it take you? Cut to Tony 25:41 “I’m talking to God” Mac “oh wow” Tony “I believe God loves music and wants somebody to play for him.”
Another short montage Tony playing sax
And he reflects on the struggles he has experienced.
Sound bite Tony.. DRIVE 2 CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW 07:59
“I was deprived of a lot of things, .. so when people deprive you of a lot of things it affects you physically, emotionally…

Inter cut with training in garden shots
Cut to Mac

All too often, his disability has led people to reject him. His first date, for instance, was traumatic.
DRIVE 2 CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW 09:08… “…“I met with a lady before in Nigeria Then I remember vividly we met. She saw me sitting down she’s like wow you look so cute I was smiling..09:36 so what really hit me bad is when I went to visit her. She saw me coming from afar, limping. She denied me. So it really hits me so hard. I went back home. I was like, okay, how can I prove myself to people?”
Cut to DRIVE HW 2 CARD 1 Mac 04:36:34 “your legs do you struggle a lot with your legs? Tony DRIVE 2 CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW 32:50 “Yeah sometimes, but I believe pain is a thing of the mind. Sometimes I feel pain but I try to like regulate it in my own mind Try to struggle it out because theres nobody to complain to so if I don’t have anybody to complain to I just got to keep on going.
Cut to interview 04;35:54 DRIVE HW 2 CARD 1 Mac “You’re going off to Cape Town. What do you hope?
DRIVE 2 CARD 4 TONY MAIN INTERVIEW 32:15
“I’m looking forward to gold medal in every activity in Cape Town. Yeah, that’s why I’ve been training hard.”

Cut to Table Mountain.. GVs of stadium…Dissolve into Montage of Tony in stadium

His disciplined training is paying off. At the championships here in Cape Town he has already done well.

Mac interaction… 3245 “Tony how you my man” “I’m good Feeling strong strong ready for my 400m You ready for your 400m? How many medals have you won so far? “I got for powerlifting” “What did you get for powerlifting?” “Gold medal”00:21 NICE Mac and Tony High Five. Tony: “On 100 I got silver.” “Mac “You got silver for 100M dash? My man!” High Five.

Cut to montage of runners competing.. especially the blind girl and her guide..

This is no ordinary sports event. Everyone here has challenges most people cannot even imagine.

This is a field where no victory is won without pain.

Cut to man coming in and falling down… him being helped and carried away on stretcher…. Let the sequence breathe without commentary…

It is a struggle where attitude and self-belief matter more than mere achievement. Most competitors’ handicaps are very different, so they are often forced to compete against themselves.

Moekie Grobbelaar, President of the South African Sports Association for the Physically Disabled, explains the unique personal challenges for Tony and for the man he shares the field with, Peter.

Interview Moekie Grobbelaar DRIVE HW 2 CAM 1 GREG 3341 04:01 “They don’t necessarily compete against each other.. each of them will compete in their own classification … because classification and disability is the backbone of our sport… so that the one is not stronger than the other because of their disability. You can never compare a paraplegic, which he is, and then Peter is a quadriplegic. So you can’t just put the two together, because I mean the muscle structures is completely different.”

Cut to Tony and his competitor Peter getting ready for the race

Cut to Mac PTC GREG CAM 1 3327 “So I guess the final moment has arrived for Tony. This is his last and final race. [He’s already won two silver medals and one gold] cut out to shorten possibly? I’m sure he’s very nervous because at this time in an athlete’s life when you get to that starting line that’s where it all counts, all the hard work all the pressure, the early mornings. This is where is really counts.”

Montage man firing starting pistol… “Get set. Bang!”

Tony and Peter race off. Cutaways crowd…

This is an odyssey into the self, a journey to find, and, ultimately, to beat, a personal best.
Tony on track…

… comes in to cross the finish line..
Cut to Mac GREG CAM 1 3329 Mac “Well here he is Tony has now gone over the finish line congratulations to him…” Mac starts clapping Tony in background..

..cut to 3330 Tony looking happy as he wheels into the stands… Tony and competitor Peter pose for photo 00:33 Tony turns to Peter “Thanks champ!”

Interview intercut over Tony and UJ teammates celebrating…

Tony and his fellow athletes each push in their own way to go just that little bit further, in their lives and on the field, not only for medals, but for the sheer pride and achievement of the very going itself.

Cut to 3338/3339 Tony and UJ team celebrating as Tony and Peter get medals hung on them 01:06 Tony hugs Peter

Cut to montage of boxing gym

But Tony has an extra, unfulfilled, dream that he also pursues.

One day, he wants to be not only a successful athlete but also South Africa’s first competitive wheelchair boxer.

Cut to interview.. “I want to do something different from what other people are doing..there’s nothing like wheelchair boxing… then I’m like if there is nothing like wheelchair boxing I will start it”

Intercut with montage of Tony sparring with boxing bag

But it’s a lonely dream, there are not many people yet who share his hopes.

So far he has found few fellow believers, and he has had only to spar against able-bodied opponents sitting in a chair.

Wheelchair boxing is growing in other countries, but has yet to be approved in South Africa.


He has a long way to go before this extra dream becomes real in his new land of opportunity, so for now, he focuses on what he can achieve.

Cut to interview 00:28:03 “I want to be a champion. A real champion. I want to motivate other people most especially people on the wheelchair. I have a lot of things to tell them about their disability. You must not, like, feel pity for yourself” Cut to Tony interview sound.... Interview sound “ 00:23:39 “I challenge myself. I don’t wait for anybody to help me… and that’s why with my sports I don’t sit for excuses..
SCRI
CUT BACK TO 22:57 when you love yourself you are good to go challenge yourself.
End shot DRIVE 1CARD 3 2227 15:21:51 CUT WITH DRONE 0030?? Pigeons fly up as Tony wheels past…

11 SECOND PROMOS

Tony Adebayo is a paraplegic sportsman who wants to be South Africa’s first wheelchair boxing champ. He believes in his dream, but now he has to persuade others to believe in him too.


Handicapped by polio, but undaunted by his limitations, Tony Adesanya is a man on a physical and spiritual odyssey to prove himself to an often hostile world and also overcome his own self-doubts.

He trains, boxes at the gym and competes in racing and weightlifting in the South African Sports Association for the Disabled championships (SASAPD) in wheelchair racing and weightlifting, keeping his many goals alive and working towards his ultimate challenge. Like all disabled people, he too, has times when things have seemed difficult, perhaps even unmanageable, but he refuses to give up. In this way he hopes to touch people's lives and inspire them to better their own and to find a way to fight for their own dreams. Living in SA for more than a decade and he sends money home to his wife and children in Nigeria, and he says South Africa is a land of opportunity, a place where he has been able to follow his dreams. Tony will be competing in the SASAPD championships in late March so we will spend a day with Tony, starting early in the morning on Friday 10 March, filming him and interviewing him as he goes about his day, from training in the early morning to playing the sax to going to the salon and the gym where he trains and boxes with other able-bodied opponents. Then on March 21 we will film him at the final day of the SASAPD championships down in Cape Town where he competes in the 800m wheelchair race and the final results are announced. He may not win the actual race, but this will provide a nice narrative arc to follow him through his journey into his own success and his personal best.
